sanskrit: tasyādya vyasane buddhiḥ saṃjāteyaṃ mamādhamā tyaktasya devair anayān mṛgayāyāṃ durātmanaḥ
english: Now in his calamity this vile resolve has arisen in me — that of one abandoned by the gods through wickedness, a wicked-souled man cast off on the hunt.

sanskrit: mokṣam eva vyavasyāmi bandho hi vyasanaṃ mahat suvṛttim anuvartiṣye tām ahaṃ pitur avyayām atīva tapasātmānaṃ yojayiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
english: I resolve upon liberation alone, for bondage is a great affliction. I shall follow that imperishable good conduct of my father, and without any doubt I shall engage myself in the most intense austerities.

sanskrit: tasmād eko 'ham ekāham ekaikasmin vanaspatau caran bhaikṣaṃ munir muṇḍaś cariṣyāmi mahīm imām
english: Therefore, alone, day by day, going from one forest tree to the next, begging alms as a shaven-headed sage, I shall wander over this earth.

sanskrit: pāṃsunā samavacchannaḥ śūnyāgārapratiśrayaḥ vṛkṣamūlaniketo vā tyaktasarvapriyāpriyaḥ
english: Covered with dust, taking shelter in empty dwellings or making my abode at the roots of trees, having abandoned all that is dear and all that is not dear.

sanskrit: na śocan na prahṛṣyaṃś ca tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ nirāśīr nirnamaskāro nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ
english: Neither grieving nor rejoicing, treating censure and self-praise as equal, without desire, without bowing to any, free from all pairs of opposites, possessing nothing.

sanskrit: na cāpy avahasan kaṃ cin na kurvan bhrukuṭīṃ kva cit prasannavadano nityaṃ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: Never mocking anyone, never knitting the brow at any time, ever serene of countenance, always devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ sarvam avihiṃsaṃś caturvidham svāsu prajāsv iva sadā samaḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ prati
english: Doing no harm to all four kinds of living beings, moving and stationary, always equal toward all that breathes as toward one's own offspring.

sanskrit: ekakālaṃ caran bhaikṣaṃ kulāni dve ca pañca ca asaṃbhave vā bhaikṣasya carann anaśanāny api
english: Begging alms only at one time of day, visiting two or five households, and when alms are not obtained, practicing fasts as well.

sanskrit: alpam alpaṃ yathābhojyaṃ pūrvalābhena jātu cit nityaṃ nāticaraṃl lābhe alābhe sapta pūrayan
english: Little by little, eating only what is fit to eat, sometimes subsisting on what was obtained before, never exceeding proper measure, filling up seven bites whether gaining or not gaining.

sanskrit: vāsyaikaṃ takṣato bāhuṃ candanenaikam ukṣataḥ nākalyāṇaṃ na kalyāṇaṃ pradhyāyann ubhayos tayoḥ
english: If one hacks at one arm with an adze and anoints the other with sandalwood paste, harboring neither ill will nor good will toward either of those two persons.

sanskrit: na jijīviṣuvat kiṃ cin na mumūrṣuvad ācaran maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ caiva nābhinandan na ca dviṣan
english: Acting neither as one who desires to live nor as one who desires to die, neither welcoming nor hating death and life.

sanskrit: yāḥ kāś cij jīvatā śakyāḥ kartum abhyudayakriyāḥ tāḥ sarvāḥ samatikramya nimeṣādiṣv avasthitaḥ
english: Passing beyond all the prospering actions that can be performed by a living being, remaining established in acts as slight as the blinking of an eye.

sanskrit: tāsu sarvāsv avasthāsu tyaktasarvendriyakriyaḥ saṃparityaktadharmātmā sunirṇiktātmakalmaṣaḥ
english: In all those states, having abandoned all activity of the senses, having wholly relinquished the sense of a dharmic self, with the impurities of the self fully cleansed.

sanskrit: nirmuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo vyatītaḥ sarvavāgurāḥ na vaśe kasya cit tiṣṭhan sadharmā mātariśvanaḥ
english: Liberated from all sins, having passed beyond all snares, not standing under anyone's sway, sharing the nature of the wind.

sanskrit: etayā satataṃ vṛttyā carann evaṃprakārayā dehaṃ saṃdhārayiṣyāmi nirbhayaṃ mārgam āsthitaḥ
english: Wandering continually with this way of life, of such a character, I shall sustain the body, having entered upon the fearless path.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ śvācarite mārge avīryakṛpaṇocite svadharmāt satatāpete rameyaṃ vīryavarjitaḥ
english: I will not delight in the path followed by a dog, fit only for the feeble and pitiable, perpetually straying from one's own duty, bereft of virility.

sanskrit: satkṛto 'saktṛto vāpi yo 'nyāṃ kṛpaṇacakṣuṣā upaiti vṛttiṃ kāmātmā sa śunāṃ vartate pathi
english: He who, whether honored or dishonored, approaches another livelihood with a miserable eye, driven by desire — he walks the path of dogs.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā suduḥkhārto niḥśvāsaparamo nṛpaḥ avekṣamāṇaḥ kuntīṃ ca mādrīṃ ca samabhāṣata
english: Vaishampayana said: Having spoken thus, the king, afflicted with great grief, sighing deeply, looking at Kunti and Madri, addressed them.

sanskrit: kausalyā viduraḥ kṣattā rājā ca saha bandhubhiḥ āryā satyavatī bhīṣmas te ca rājapurohitāḥ
english: Kaushalya, Vidura the Kshattar, the king together with his kinsmen, the venerable Satyavati, Bhishma, and the royal priests —

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś ca mahātmānaḥ somapāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ pauravṛddhāś ca ye tatra nivasanty asmadāśrayāḥ prasādya sarve vaktavyāḥ pāṇḍuḥ pravrajito vanam
english: And the great-souled Brahmanas, drinkers of soma, of sharpened vows, and the elders of the Pauravas who dwell there under our protection — all of them are to be propitiated and told: Pandu has gone forth to the forest.

sanskrit: niśamya vacanaṃ bhartur vanavāse dhṛtātmanaḥ tatsamaṃ vacanaṃ kuntī mādrī ca samabhāṣatām
english: Having heard the words of their husband whose mind was resolved upon forest-dwelling, Kunti and Madri both spoke words equal to his own.

sanskrit: anye 'pi hy āśramāḥ santi ye śakyā bharatarṣabha āvābhyāṃ dharmapatnībhyāṃ saha taptvā tapo mahat tvam eva bhavitā sārthaḥ svargasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ
english: O bull of the Bharatas, there are also other ashramas that are possible; if we, your two lawful wives, perform great austerities together with you, you will assuredly be rewarded — even as regards heaven, there is no doubt.

sanskrit: praṇidhāyendriyagrāmaṃ bhartṛlokaparāyaṇe tyaktakāmasukhe hy āvāṃ tapsyāvo vipulaṃ tapaḥ
english: Restraining the entire host of our senses, devoted to the world of our husband, having abandoned the pleasures of desire, we two shall practice abundant austerity.

sanskrit: yadi āvāṃ mahāprājña tyakṣyasi tvaṃ viśāṃ pate adyaivāvāṃ prahāsyāvo jītivaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: O greatly wise one, O lord of men, if you abandon us two, this very day we two shall abandon life — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca yadi vyavasitaṃ hy etad yuvayor dharmasaṃhitam svavṛttim anuvartiṣye tām ahaṃ pitur avyayām
english: Pandu said: If this resolve of yours two is in conformity with dharma, then I shall follow that imperishable way of conduct of my father.

sanskrit: tyaktagrāmyasukhācāras tapyamāno mahat tapaḥ valkalī phalamūlāśī cariṣyāmi mahāvane
english: Having abandoned the practices and pleasures of village life, performing great austerity, wearing bark garments, eating fruits and roots, I shall wander in the great forest.

sanskrit: agniṃ juhvann ubhau kālāv ubhau kālāv upaspṛśan kṛśaḥ parimitāhāraś cīracarmajaṭādharaḥ
english: Offering oblations into the fire at both twilights, touching water at both twilights, lean, taking limited food, wearing rags and hides and matted locks.

sanskrit: śītavātātapasahaḥ kṣutpipāsāśramānvitaḥ tapasā duścareṇedaṃ śarīram upaśoṣayan
english: Enduring cold, wind, and heat, accompanied by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, drying out this body with austerity that is hard to perform.

sanskrit: ekāntaśīlī vimṛśan pakvāpakvena vartayan pitṝn devāṃś ca vanyena vāgbhir adbhiś ca tarpayan
english: Inclined to solitude, reflecting, subsisting on cooked and uncooked food alike, satisfying the ancestors and gods with forest offerings, with words, and with water.

sanskrit: vānaprasthajanasyāpi darśanaṃ kulavāsinām nāpriyāṇy ācarañ jātu kiṃ punar grāmavāsinām
english: Never performing disagreeable acts even toward forest-dwelling persons and those who dwell in hermitages — how much less toward those who dwell in villages.

sanskrit: evam āraṇyaśāstrāṇām ugram ugrataraṃ vidhim kāṅkṣamāṇo 'ham āsiṣye dehasyāsya samāpanāt
english: Thus desiring the fierce, yet fiercer rule prescribed by the forest treatises, I shall abide until this body is extinguished.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity evam uktvā bhārye te rājā kauravavaṃśajaḥ tataś cūḍāmaṇiṃ niṣkam aṅgade kuṇḍalāni ca vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi strīṇām ābharaṇāni ca
english: Vaishampayana said: Having thus spoken to those two wives of his, the king born of the Kaurava lineage then gave the crest-jewel, the neck-ornament, the armlets, the earrings, costly garments, and women's ornaments —

sanskrit: pradāya sarvaṃ viprebhyaḥ pāṇḍuḥ punar abhāṣata gatvā nāgapuraṃ vācyaṃ pāṇḍuḥ pravrajito vanam
english: Having given all of these to the Brahmanas, Pandu spoke again: Going to Nagapura, it should be announced — Pandu has gone forth to the forest.

sanskrit: arthaṃ kāmaṃ sukhaṃ caiva ratiṃ ca paramātmikām pratasthe sarvam utsṛjya sabhāryaḥ kurupuṃgavaḥ
english: Having abandoned all wealth, desire, pleasure, and the supreme delight of the self, the bull of the Kurus set out with his wives.

sanskrit: tatas tasyānuyātrāṇi te caiva paricārakāḥ śrutvā bharatasiṃhasya vividhāḥ karuṇā giraḥ bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ kṛtvā hāheti paricukruśuḥ
english: Then his retinue and those attendants, hearing the various pitiful words of that lion of the Bharatas, cried out in a terrible, anguished voice: "Alas! Alas!"

sanskrit: uṣṇam aśru vimuñcantas taṃ vihāya mahīpatim yayur nāgapuraṃ tūrṇaṃ sarvam ādāya tadvacaḥ
english: Shedding hot tears, abandoning that lord of the earth, they went swiftly to Nagapura, carrying all of his message.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca tebhyas tat sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ mahāvane dhṛtarāṣṭro naraśreṣṭhaḥ pāṇḍum evānvaśocata
english: And having heard from them all that had happened in the great forest, Dhritarashtra, foremost of men, grieved for Pandu alone.

sanskrit: rājaputras tu kauravyaḥ pāṇḍur mūlaphalāśanaḥ jagāma saha bhāryābhyāṃ tato nāgasabhaṃ girim
english: The prince of the Kauravas, Pandu, subsisting on roots and fruits, then went together with his wives to the mountain Nagasabha.

sanskrit: sa caitraratham āsādya vāriṣeṇam atītya ca himavantam atikramya prayayau gandhamādanam
english: Reaching the Chaitraratha, passing beyond Varishena, crossing the Himavat, he journeyed on to the Gandhamadana.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇo mahābhūtaiḥ siddhaiś ca paramarṣibhiḥ uvāsa sa tadā rājā sameṣu viṣameṣu ca
english: Protected by the great spirits and by the Siddhas and supreme sages, the king then dwelt in level and uneven places alike.

sanskrit: indradyumnasaraḥ prāpya haṃsakūṭam atītya ca śataśṛṅge mahārāja tāpasaḥ samapadyata
english: O great king, having reached the lake Indradyumna and passed beyond Hamshakoota, he became an ascetic on the Shatashringa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatrāpi tapasi śreṣṭhe vartamānaḥ sa vīryavān siddhacāraṇasaṃghānāṃ babhūva priyadarśanaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Even there, engaged in the highest austerity, that mighty one became a beloved sight to the hosts of Siddhas and Charanas.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣur anahaṃvādī saṃyatātmā jitendriyaḥ svargaṃ gantuṃ parākrāntaḥ svena vīryeṇa bhārata
english: Devoted to service, free from arrogance, self-controlled, his senses conquered, striving to reach heaven through his own prowess, O Bharata.

sanskrit: keṣāṃ cid abhavad bhrātā keṣāṃ cid abhavat sakhā ṛṣayas tv apare cainaṃ putravat paryapālayan
english: To some he became a brother, to others a friend; and other sages protected him as if he were a son.

sanskrit: sa tu kālena mahatā prāpya niṣkalmaṣaṃ tapaḥ brahmarṣisadṛśaḥ pāṇḍur babhūva bharatarṣabha
english: But after a long time, having attained stainless austerity, Pandu became like a Brahmarishi, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: svargapāraṃ titīrṣan sa śataśṛṅgād udaṅmukhaḥ pratasthe saha patnībhyām abruvaṃs tatra tāpasāḥ upary upari gacchantaḥ śailarājam udaṅmukhāḥ
english: Desiring to cross to the far shore of heaven, he set forth with his wives from Shatashringa, facing north; but the ascetics there spoke to him as they went up and ever further up the king of mountains, facing north.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭavanto girer asya durgān deśān bahūn vayam ākrīḍabhūtān devānāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā
english: We have seen many impassable regions of this mountain — the playgrounds of the gods and likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

sanskrit: udyānāni kuberasya samāni viṣamāṇi ca mahānadīnitambāṃś ca durgāṃś ca girigahvarān
english: The gardens of Kubera, level and uneven; the banks of great rivers; impassable places and mountain caverns.

sanskrit: santi nityahimā deśā nirvṛkṣamṛgapakṣiṇaḥ santi ke cin mahāvarṣā durgāḥ ke cid durāsadāḥ
english: There are regions of perpetual snow, devoid of trees, beasts, and birds; some places of great downpour; some that are impassable; some that are hard to reach.

sanskrit: atikrāmen na pakṣī yān kuta evetare mṛgāḥ vāyur eko 'tigād yatra siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: No bird can cross those places, let alone other animals; only the wind passes through there, and the Siddhas and supreme sages.

sanskrit: gacchantyau śailarāje 'smin rājaputryau kathaṃ tv ime na sīdetām aduḥkhārhe mā gamo bharatarṣabha
english: On this king of mountains, how could these two royal ladies walking there not falter? O bull of the Bharatas, you who do not deserve suffering — do not go.

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca aprajasya mahābhāgā na dvāraṃ paricakṣate svarge tenābhitapto 'ham aprajas tad bravīmi vaḥ
english: Pandu said: O greatly fortunate ones, the gate to heaven is not declared open for one without offspring. Tormented by that, I who am without offspring — this I tell you.

sanskrit: ṛṇaiś caturbhiḥ saṃyuktā jāyante manujā bhuvi pitṛdevarṣimanujadeyaiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: Men are born on earth bound by four debts — the debts owed to ancestors, gods, sages, and men — by the hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: etāni tu yathākālaṃ yo na budhyati mānavaḥ na tasya lokāḥ santīti dharmavidbhiḥ pratiṣṭhitam
english: But those who do not discharge these in due time — for them there are no higher worlds: this has been established by those who know dharma.

sanskrit: yajñaiś ca devān prīṇāti svādhyāyatapasā munīn putraiḥ śrāddhaiḥ pitṝṃś cāpi ānṛśaṃsyena mānavān
english: One satisfies the gods through sacrifices, sages through study and austerity, ancestors through sons and funeral rites, and men through kindness.

sanskrit: ṛṣidevamanuṣyāṇāṃ parimukto 'smi dharmataḥ pitryād ṛṇād anirmuktas tena tapye tapodhanāḥ
english: From the debt to sages, gods, and men I am free by dharma; but from the debt to the ancestors I am not free — and by that I am tormented, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: dehanāśe dhruvo nāśaḥ pitṝṇām eṣa niścayaḥ iha tasmāt prajāhetoḥ prajāyante narottamāḥ
english: When the body perishes, the ancestors perish with certainty — this is the settled truth. Therefore the best of men are born here for the purpose of offspring.

sanskrit: yathaivāhaṃ pituḥ kṣetre sṛṣṭas tena mahātmanā tathaivāsmin mama kṣetre kathaṃ vai saṃbhavet prajā
english: Just as I was created by that great soul in my father's field, so how indeed might offspring come to be in this field of mine?

sanskrit: tāpasā ūcuḥ asti vai tava dharmātman vidma devopamaṃ śubham apatyam anaghaṃ rājan vayaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā
english: The ascetics said: O man of dharma, O king, there is indeed auspicious, sinless offspring for you equal to the gods — this we know with divine sight.

sanskrit: daivadiṣṭaṃ naravyāghra karmaṇehopapādaya akliṣṭaṃ phalam avyagro vindate buddhimān naraḥ
english: O tiger among men, bring about here through action what is ordained by fate; a wise man, untroubled, obtains fruit without hardship.

sanskrit: tasmin dṛṣṭe phale tāta prayatnaṃ kartum arhasi apatyaṃ guṇasaṃpannaṃ labdhvā prītim avāpsyasi
english: When the fruit is thus seen, dear one, you should make the effort; having obtained offspring endowed with virtues, you will attain joy.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā tāpasavacaḥ pāṇḍuś cintāparo 'bhavat ātmano mṛgaśāpena jānann upahatāṃ kriyām
english: Vaishampayana said: Having heard those words of the ascetics, Pandu became deeply anxious, knowing that his own capacity for begetting had been destroyed by the curse of the deer.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd vijane kuntīṃ dharmapatnīṃ yaśasvinīm apatyotpādane yogam āpadi prasamarthayan
english: He spoke in private to Kunti, his lawful wife of great renown, deliberating on the means for producing offspring in this difficult situation.

sanskrit: apatyaṃ nāma lokeṣu pratiṣṭhā dharmasaṃhitā iti kunti vidur dhīrāḥ śāśvataṃ dharmam āditaḥ
english: Offspring, O Kunti, is indeed the foundation in the worlds, joined to dharma — thus the wise have known from the beginning as the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ niyamaś ca svanuṣṭhitaḥ sarvam evānapatyasya na pāvanam ihocyate
english: The sacrifice performed, the gift given, the austerity practiced, the vow duly observed — all of this is said here to bring no purification for the one without offspring.

sanskrit: so 'ham evaṃ viditvaitat prapaśyāmi śucismite anapatyaḥ śubhāṃl lokān nāvāpsyāmīti cintayan
english: Knowing this, O bright-smiling one, I see clearly, reflecting that I who am without offspring shall not attain the auspicious worlds.

sanskrit: mṛgābhiśāpān naṣṭaṃ me prajanaṃ hy akṛtātmanaḥ nṛśaṃsakāriṇo bhīru yathaivopahataṃ tathā
english: My power of begetting has been destroyed by the curse of the deer, O timid one, for me of unrestrained self, a perpetrator of cruelty — destroyed as thoroughly as if it had been shattered.

sanskrit: ime vai bandhudāyādāḥ ṣaṭ putrā dharmadarśane ṣaḍ evābandhudāyādāḥ putrās tāñ śṛṇu me pṛthe
english: In the view of dharma there are indeed six types of sons who are heirs of kinsmen, and six who are not heirs of kinsmen — hear them from me, O Pritha.

sanskrit: svayaṃjātaḥ praṇītaś ca parikrītaś ca yaḥ sutaḥ paunarbhavaś ca kānīnaḥ svairiṇyāṃ yaś ca jāyate
english: The self-born, the appointed, and the purchased son; the son of a remarried woman, the son born before marriage, and he who is born of a woman who goes freely.

sanskrit: dattaḥ krītaḥ kṛtrimaś ca upagacchet svayaṃ ca yaḥ sahoḍho jātaretāś ca hīnayonidhṛtaś ca yaḥ
english: The given, the bought, the adopted, and he who comes of his own accord; one carried in the womb at the time of marriage, one born from seed already deposited, and one maintained from a low womb.

sanskrit: pūrvapūrvatamābhāve matvā lipseta vai sutam uttamād avarāḥ puṃsaḥ kāṅkṣante putram āpadi
english: In the absence of the prior and the most prior, understanding this, one should desire to obtain a son; inferior men seek a son from a superior man in adversity.

sanskrit: apatyaṃ dharmaphaladaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vindanti sādhavaḥ ātmaśukrād api pṛthe manuḥ svāyambhuvo 'bravīt
english: The good obtain the finest offspring that yields the fruit of dharma even from another's seed, O Pritha — so declared Manu Svayambhuva.

sanskrit: tasmāt praheṣyāmy adya tvāṃ hīnaḥ prajananāt svayam sadṛśāc chreyaso vā tvaṃ viddhy apatyaṃ yaśasvini
english: Therefore today I shall send you out, I myself being deficient in the power of begetting — know the offspring to be your own, O renowned one, from one equal to me or superior.

sanskrit: śṛṇu kunti kathāṃ cemāṃ śāradaṇḍāyanīṃ prati yā vīrapatnī gurubhir niyuktāpatyajanmani
english: Hear also this story, O Kunti, concerning Sharadandayani, that wife of a hero who was appointed by her elders for the birth of offspring.

sanskrit: puṣpeṇa prayatā snātā niśi kunti catuṣpathe varayitvā dvijaṃ siddhaṃ hutvā puṃsavane 'nalam
english: Purified in her season and bathed, O Kunti, at night at a crossroads, having chosen a perfected twice-born and offered oblations into the fire at the son-producing rite —

sanskrit: karmaṇy avasite tasmin sā tenaiva sahāvasat tatra trīñ janayām āsa durjayādīn mahārathān
english: When that rite was concluded, she dwelt together with him; there she gave birth to three great warriors beginning with Durjaya.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api kalyāṇi brāhmaṇāt tapasādhikāt manniyogād yata kṣipram apatyotpādanaṃ prati
english: In the same way, O auspicious one, by my command, go quickly to a Brahmin distinguished in austerity for the production of offspring.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktā mahārāja kuntī pāṇḍum abhāṣata kurūṇām ṛṣabhaṃ vīraṃ tadā bhūmipatiṃ patim
english: Vaishampayana said: O great king, thus addressed, Kunti spoke to Pandu, that bull of the Kurus, the brave lord of the earth, her husband.

sanskrit: na mām arhasi dharmajña vaktum evaṃ kathaṃ cana dharmapatnīm abhiratāṃ tvayi rājīvalocana
english: O knower of dharma, O lotus-eyed one, you should not speak to me like this in any way — to me your lawful wife who delights in you.

sanskrit: tvam eva tu mahābāho mayy apatyāni bhārata vīra vīryopapannāni dharmato janayiṣyasi
english: Rather, O mighty-armed one, O hero, O Bharata, you yourself shall beget on me offspring endowed with valor, in accordance with dharma.
